findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, which get_event_stats_factory may replace (e.g. dashboard discover-split passes split_dataset=discover or the original scoped dataset), but the eligibility check passes the closure variable `dataset` instead. The transform decision therefore does not describe the dataset actually queried: split/error queries can miss upsampling and transaction-like split queries can be transformed based on the wrong dataset, producing wrong counts or invalid sample_weight queries.

findings.title: upsampled_count is enabled for the errors dataset but only registered in Discover
findings.body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for sentry.snuba.errors, so count() is rewritten to upsampled_count() for dataset=errors requests. The new SnQLFunction is only added to Discover's function_converter in src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py; the errors dataset has its own function converter and does not gain this function from that change. Errors-dataset timeseries requests for allowlisted projects will fail function resolution instead of returning upsampled counts.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) undercounts events whose sample_weight is NULL
findings.body: The aggregate is sum(sample_weight) with no coalesce/fallback. Events stored before client error sampling was populated, or events without a sample rate, can have NULL sample_weight; ClickHouse sum ignores NULLs, so those events contribute 0 instead of 1. Once any allowlisted project is queried, historical/unsampled errors silently disappear from count() results instead of counting with weight 1 (e.g. sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))).

findings.title: Substring check treats negated/non-error queries as error-focused
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query returns True whenever the raw query text contains 'event.type:error', including '!event.type:error' (explicitly excluding errors), quoted/tag values containing that text, or a broader OR query that also includes transactions. For Discover this incorrectly rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight) for transaction/non-error results, yielding wrong totals or queries against rows without meaningful sample_weight. The parsed query conditions, not a substring search, need to establish that results are errors only.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public user-callable function
findings.body: Unlike the internal count helpers around it, the new SnQLFunction is not marked private=True. Any user can therefore send yAxis=upsampled_count() directly on any Discover query/project, bypassing the endpoint's all-projects-allowlisted and error-only checks. On transaction queries this can fail on sample_weight or return misleading weighted counts; the function should be private so only the server-side rewrite can invoke it.

findings.title: Cache key compresses project IDs into a single hash value
findings.body: Eligibility is cached under hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))) rather than the project IDs themselves. Different project sets whose tuple hash collides share one cached allowlist verdict for 60s, so a non-allowlisted set can be treated as allowlisted (or vice versa) and counts are silently weighted/unweighted incorrectly. invalidate_upsampling_cache repeats the same scheme and cannot disambiguate. Build the key from the joined sorted IDs instead of a lossy hash.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink file added to the repository root
findings.body: The PR adds a new root entry 'sentry-repo' containing 'Subproject commit a5d2909...', i.e. an accidental nested-repo gitlink rather than application code. Merging it creates a stray submodule-like entry without .gitmodules metadata, which breaks/clutters checkouts and tooling; it should be removed from the change.
